floor_history.headline: Recon: stale 119 migration pin killed — honest floor is 57/173 (insn-count already exact); residual is one OR-association copy + the count-1 comparand carrier, both pass-attributed from the .loop dump

Floor 57 -> 52 in pure ordinary C: declaring `complement` inside the inner loop spends loop.c's first move (threshold -= 3) so the `count - 1` comparand stays inline, which retires s1's variable-reuse

Floor 52 -> 31 in ordinary C: fold-const's associate: block aims the OR-chain constant (write it next to the OTHER term), a late `i = 0;` fixes the $s1/$s2 pair, and one arm-local `*dst++` swaps the s

Seat question re-framed from the target's own asm: the TARGET compiles with the same weighted reg_n_refs we do (src 32 / dst 26), so the banked 'refs move on pseudo 109' framing is not how the origina

frontier.hypothesis: The refs_up atom on dst (26 -> 32) can be bought without losing the 173rd instruction if the duplicated statement lands in arms whose TAILS are not byte-identical, so jump2 has nothing to cross-jump.
frontier.mechanism: inverse.py's own catalog names duplicated-statement-into-arms (SANCTIONED, .claude/rules/duplicated-statement-into-arms.md, FAKE-annotated) as the byte-free reg_n_refs lift for exactly this global-RA priority wall. Every dose measured so far (s3 d2/d3/d5/d6, s6 k8) duplicates the dst increment into an arm whose tail then matches the colour arm's `sh / addiu a2 / j loop_check / addiu a3` exactly, and jump2's cross_jump merges it. A duplication placed BEFORE the store, or into arms that jump to different labels, gives jump2 no common suffix.
frontier.next_probe: On the k1 chassis, enumerate duplications that raise dst's weighted refs by 6 while leaving the four arm tails pairwise distinct: (i) duplicate the dst store (not the increment) into the blend main path and the colour arm with different following labels; (ii) put the extra dst reference before the `sh` rather than after it; (iii) split `advance_dst: dst++;` so the two zero arms reach it through different labels. Gate every form on `build_insns == 173` FIRST - a 172-insn result is the same dead end as k8 and needs no further analysis - then read the seat with tools/ra_solver simulate --trace. Only if a 173-insn form with dst refs >= 32 exists is the FAKE paperwork (scope sentence quoted from the rule, SOTN precedent, exhaustion ledger) worth writing.

frontier.hypothesis: The mirror atom - src 32 -> 26 weighted refs - is buyable by removing exactly one `addiu a3,a3,2` from the inner loop while keeping 173 instructions, if the removal leaves the remaining arms' `j`s with delay-slot fillers.
frontier.mechanism: s4 killed the two natural hoists (g1 = 61 / 162, g2 = 48 / 166) because moving the read and/or all four increments to the top of the do-body leaves reorg.c nothing to fill three `j` delay slots with, losing 7-11 instructions. That is an argument against hoisting ALL of them, not against removing ONE. Removing one increment is -2 RTL refs at depth 3 = -6 weighted, which is exactly the atom.
frontier.next_probe: On the k1 chassis, measure forms that share ONE `src++` between exactly two arms while the other two keep their own: (i) `advance_dst: dst++; src++;` with the colour arm and the blend main path keeping their own increments; (ii) the last-frame branch's two arms sharing a single `u16 pixel = *src++;` while the blend branch keeps its two. Check `build_insns` before anything else; if a form holds 173, extract the model and check refs on pseudo 108 and the seat.

frontier.hypothesis: The blend arm's emission order - now the largest single block in the h1/k1 residual - is a first-pass sched.c ordering, not a spelling, and is separable from the seat.
frontier.mechanism: The target emits all six mult/mflo pairs and both channel adds before it starts the OR chain (8003DF8C-8003E020); our builds interleave an `or` after each channel. sched.c's list scheduler runs before local/global allocation, so this ordering is also an input to the allocation that produces the seat - which is why k1's extra named intermediate moved the seat at all. s5 exhausted the naming/declaration-order/operand-order axes on this block, so more spellings are not the tool.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/sched_solver on the k1 chassis against the target's blend-arm order (it is order- and clock-exact and reproduces both scheduler passes), and use inverse_sched.py to get ranked C-lever vectors for the specific insn pairs that differ. Treat any verdict as a hypothesis until a spelled C form measures; the point of the run is to say whether the ordering is REACHABLE at all before another session spends itself on it.
